current_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens where the curse reverses generational direction: יִזָּכֵ֤ר עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו (web:Ps.109.14 = oshb:Ps.109.14, “Let the iniquity of his fathers be remembered”) turns from web:Ps.109.9-Ps.109.13’s forward-looking curses on his children and his posterity to the wicked man’s fathers and mother. A shared remembrance-root binds oshb:Ps.109.14-Ps.109.16: the verb opening יִזָּכֵ֤ר עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו recurs as the noun זִכְרָֽם (web:Ps.109.15 = oshb:Ps.109.15, “their memory”) and again in the motive clause יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹ֥א זָכַר֮ (web:Ps.109.16 = oshb:Ps.109.16, “because he didn’t remember”). The curse then resumes as a clothing image: וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ב קְ֭לָלָה (web:Ps.109.17 = oshb:Ps.109.17, “he loved cursing”) and וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ קְלָלָ֗ה (web:Ps.109.18 = oshb:Ps.109.18, “He clothed himself also with cursing”)—the cursing-noun shared by both verses is otherwise unattested in the book (sweep: 2 of 2 skeleton hits book-wide, both here). The unit closes on the verdict-label זֹ֤את פְּעֻלַּ֣ת שֹׂ֭טְנַי מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה (web:Ps.109.20 = oshb:Ps.109.20, “This is the reward of my adversaries from Yahweh”), reverting to the plural “my adversaries” of web:Ps.109.1-Ps.109.5 before the direct petition opens at web:Ps.109.21.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting off the motive clause and clothing image (web:Ps.109.16-Ps.109.20) as its own row was considered but rejected because the shared remembrance-root binds web:Ps.109.16 too tightly to web:Ps.109.14-Ps.109.15 to argue an independent seam.

a shared remembrance-root recurs across three verses in sequence: יִזָּכֵ֤ר עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו (oshb:Ps.109.14), זִכְרָֽם (oshb:Ps.109.15), יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹ֥א זָכַר֮ (oshb:Ps.109.16)
the cursing-noun shared by both verses occurs only at oshb:Ps.109.17 and Ps.109.18 book-wide (sweep: 2 of 2 skeleton hits)
demonstrative opens the closing verdict clause זֹ֤את פְּעֻלַּ֣ת שֹׂ֭טְנַי מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה at oshb:Ps.109.20
current_row.device_notes: The clothing-as-curse image (web:Ps.109.17-Ps.109.19) is this psalm’s own device, not shared with the other five psalms of this span.

items.claim: The row mis-states the grammar of the neighbouring span in device_notes, incompatibly with the embedded next row, and mis-states the extent of the curse-chain it argues in boundary_rationale.
auditor_grounds: device_notes asserts that the imprecatory register continues into web:Ps.109.14-Ps.109.20 'under different grammar (a motive clause replaces the jussive chain there)'. The bytes contradict the replacement: MT 109:14 opens יִזָּכֵ֤ר, MT 109:15 opens יִהְי֣וּ, and MT 109:19 opens תְּהִי — all jussive — while the motive clause יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר stands at MT 109:16 alone. The embedded neighbour row M8-Ps-371 argues that same span FROM יִזָּכֵ֤ר as its opening jussive and treats יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר as one member of a remembrance-root chain, so the two rows characterise 109:14-20 incompatibly. Separately, boundary_rationale calls the chain 'bounded by a fatherless-root inclusio' at oshb:Ps.109.9 and oshb:Ps.109.12, but that pair bounds neither the row's span (Ps.109.6-Ps.109.13) nor the chain, which is already jussive at MT 109:8 (יִֽהְיֽוּ) after the imperative הַפְקֵ֣ד at MT 109:6 and is still jussive at the row's own closing verse, MT 109:13 יְהִֽי אַחֲרִית֥וֹ לְהַכְרִ֑ית. Not alone load-bearing: the 13|14 seam stands on the byte-true generational reversal at MT 109:14 (אֲ֭בֹתָיו).
items.proposed_change: Field repair, no respan. device_notes: replace 'a motive clause replaces the jussive chain there' with the byte-true differentiator — the kinship reversal to אֲ֭בֹתָיו at MT 109:14, with the motive clause located at MT 109:16 only. boundary_rationale: describe oshb:Ps.109.9 / oshb:Ps.109.12 as an interior fatherless-root echo rather than a bounding inclusio. Seam-pair discipline: any device_notes cure is installed on both M8-Ps-370 and M8-Ps-371.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes: Psalm 109 is identity-numbered and titled (web:Ps.109.0 is the prefix of oshb:Ps.109.1; 31 WEB = 31 MT verses; the row's dual-cites check via ps_lib). FINDING TESTED AGAINST THE ROW, claim 1: device_notes says the imprecatory register continues into web:Ps.109.14-Ps.109.20 'under different grammar (a motive clause replaces the jussive chain there)'. Bytes: oshb:Ps.109.14 opens יִזָּכֵ֤ר עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו and closes אַל תִּמָּֽח (a jussive-force imperfect and a negative jussive); oshb:Ps.109.15 opens יִהְי֣וּ (jussive force); oshb:Ps.109.19 opens תְּהִי (apocopated jussive); the motive particle יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר stands at oshb:Ps.109.16 alone, its clause continued by the wayyiqtols וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ב (oshb:Ps.109.17) and וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ (oshb:Ps.109.18) before תְּהִי resumes the curse and זֹ֤את פְּעֻלַּ֣ת (oshb:Ps.109.20) closes on a verdict label. The jussive chain does NOT stop at the seam and no motive clause 'replaces' it: the claim is byte-false. E-18 arm: the embedded neighbor M8-Ps-371 argues that very span FROM יִזָּכֵ֤ר עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו as its opening curse and treats יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר as one member of a remembrance chain, so the two rows characterise oshb:Ps.109.14-Ps.109.20 incompatibly - a false cross-row claim, medium under the register-lane law. Claim 2: boundary_rationale says the jussive chain is 'bounded by a fatherless-root inclusio' at oshb:Ps.109.9 and oshb:Ps.109.12 while itself opening the chain at יִֽהְיֽוּ (oshb:Ps.109.8) after the imperative הַפְקֵ֣ד (oshb:Ps.109.6) and closing the unit at יְהִֽי אַחֲרִית֥וֹ לְהַכְרִ֑ית (oshb:Ps.109.13): יְתוֹמִ֑ים (oshb:Ps.109.9) and לִיתוֹמָֽיו (oshb:Ps.109.12) are interior to both the span (109.6-13) and the chain (109.8-13), so 'bounded ... inclusio' mis-types an interior echo as a bracketing device. The row's two sweep digits for the pair re-derive true (skeleton of the 109.9 spelling: 3 verses book-wide, oshb:Ps.68.6, 94.6, 109.9, so 2 outside the span; the suffixed spelling of 109.12: 1 verse book-wide), so the digits are sound and only the device label is wrong. ROW TESTED AGAINST THE FINDING: neither seam rests on the defective claims - the front edge stands on the singular עָלָ֣יו at oshb:Ps.109.6 after the third-plural forms of oshb:Ps.109.2-Ps.109.5 (re-derived true), and the rear edge on the generational reversal at oshb:Ps.109.14 (אֲ֭בֹתָיו, אִ֝מּ֗וֹ) - so medium, not high; not low, because a byte-false grammatical claim about the neighbor's span plus a mis-typed device are evidence defects, not register slips. BOTH SIDES of the seam web:Ps.109.13|web:Ps.109.14 from bytes: oshb:Ps.109.13 closes יִמַּ֥ח שְׁמָֽם and oshb:Ps.109.14 opens יִזָּכֵ֤ר עֲוֺ֣ן אֲ֭בֹתָיו - both jussive, and the same blot-out root closes both verses (יִמַּ֥ח at 109.13, אַל תִּמָּֽח at 109.14) - so no grammatical device closes a unit at 109.13; what decides the seam is the kinship-direction turn from posterity to fathers and mother, a content seam inside one continuous jussive chain, with no section 5 speaker/addressee shift until וְאַתָּ֤ה יְה֘וִ֤ה אֲדֹנָ֗י opens the direct petition at oshb:Ps.109.21; both rows hold it honestly at medium. REPAIR PROPOSAL validated adversarially and endorsed WITH QUALIFICATION: replacing the device_notes clause with the kinship reversal at oshb:Ps.109.14 is byte-sound, but 'the motive clause located at MT 109:16 only' should read that the motive PARTICLE stands at oshb:Ps.109.16 only, its clause running through the wayyiqtols of oshb:Ps.109.17-18 before the jussive resumes at oshb:Ps.109.19; re-describing 109.9/109.12 as an interior fatherless echo is endorsed as written; the seam-pair discipline (one cure installed on both M8-Ps-370 and M8-Ps-371) is endorsed. Marks: no K/Q in oshb:Ps.109.6-Ps.109.21 (pmarks_Ps.json kq); paseq at oshb:Ps.109.14, 109.16 and 109.21 count-only, not relied on; no Selah in Psalm 109 (word-bound sweep). span_change false, so span_ruling n/a. Same-model-family caveat: this adjudicator is the same Anthropic family as the auditor, so agreement here is one correlated M8 voice, corroboration only, never independent confirmation.

seam_pair_partner_repaired_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens at web:Ps.109.6 where an unmarked singular “him” replaces the plural accusers of the preceding row—הַפְקֵ֣ד עָלָ֣יו רָשָׁ֑ע (web:Ps.109.6 = oshb:Ps.109.6, “Set a wicked man over him”)—and no reported-speech verb (a 'saying' or 'who say' construction) introduces the shift; on the frame bytes this reads as the psalmist continuing his own prayer against a singular, representative adversary rather than resuming a quotation of the accusers’ own words. A jussive curse-chain runs unbroken through the span, opening יִֽהְיֽוּ (oshb:Ps.109.8) and carrying an interior fatherless-root echo: בָנָ֥יו יְתוֹמִ֑ים (web:Ps.109.9 = oshb:Ps.109.9, “his children be fatherless”) and, echoing it, ח֝וֹנֵ֗ן לִיתוֹמָֽיו (web:Ps.109.12 = oshb:Ps.109.12, “no one to extend kindness...to have pity on his fatherless children”)—two distinct fatherless-root spellings, swept separately: 109:9's spelling recurs in 3 verses book-wide (2 outside this span); 109:12's spelling is unique to 109:12 book-wide (1 verse), inside this span. The unit closes on יְהִֽי אַחֲרִית֥וֹ לְהַכְרִ֑ית (web:Ps.109.13 = oshb:Ps.109.13, “Let his posterity be cut off”).
seam_pair_partner_repaired_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A minority reading takes web:Ps.109.6-Ps.109.19 as the psalmist quoting the very curse his accusers pronounced against him—resuming, after the intervening description, the reported speech flagged by web:Ps.109.2’s “They have spoken to me with a lying tongue” so that the singular “him” is the psalmist himself. The Hebrew supplies no quotation-opening verb at the web:Ps.109.5|Ps.109.6 seam to settle the question, so this rival is a live, byte-honest alternative, not excluded by the frame.

seam_pair_partner_repaired_row.device_notes: The jussive curse-chain opening here is the psalm's most-debated internal seam; its imprecatory register continues into web:Ps.109.14-Ps.109.20 under the same jussive grammar apart from the motive particle יַ֗עַן אֲשֶׁ֤ר at oshb:Ps.109.16 alone, whose clause runs through the wayyiqtols of oshb:Ps.109.17-18 (וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ב, וַיִּלְבַּ֥שׁ) before the jussive resumes at oshb:Ps.109.19 (תְּהִי), the kinship reversal to אֲ֭בֹתָיו (oshb:Ps.109.14) marking the turn.
